entries.title: Hunt opened
entries.body: Frame dips below 20 fps while walking and a steady 17 to 21 ms render call. Two plans written and reviewed by Astra: terrain streaming integration and render submission. Two Opus agents implement; every commit reviewed in comms.txt.

entries.title: Terrain steps 1 to 6 and render trace flags
entries.body: Worker-side tint, bounded inbox, one 2 ms soft-deadline scheduler, prefetch and hysteresis, shared in-flight cap. ?trace=1 render trace, ?matrixauto=0 (no gain, closed), ?bundles=1 (afterimage, closed).

entries.title: Dips tied to terrain worker contention
entries.body: DevTools trace: 16 terrain threads, 104 of 106 long frames overlapped a burst. Shared worker pool replaced them. Within a capture, 4 busy workers ran a frame at 61 ms against 28 idle; 2 busy ran 17.6 against 17.7. Default cap set to 2 at the user's word. Astra's feedback on overclaiming recorded.

entries.title: Architecture review, two revisions
entries.body: Six Sonnet read-only reports plus material-ownership and BatchedMesh follow-ups. Three report claims failed on code read (matrix-walk figure, terrain cull default, margin chunk count); one of mine did too (BatchedMesh lives in three.core.js). Verdict revised: bindings ~38% of render samples; the rest unnamed at sub-phase level.

entries.title: Implementation round 1
entries.body: Sub-phase render trace with counters; craft material cache; terrain upload accounting and residency; grass clock and origin uniforms to the render group; forest consolidation design; binding ownership inventory (the env-intensity finding did not apply here).

entries.title: Round 2: lifetimes, sets, mechanics
entries.body: Craft materials reference counted instead of a no-op dispose; residency as key sets; grass uniform mechanics tested against the shipped NodeFrame with a runtime option and ?grassScope=object; forest census settled at 16 variants and the slot-mapped pulled prototype behind a default-off select.

entries.title: First captures with the stage split
entries.body: Encode 12 to 42 ms; bindings ~45%, nodes ~17%. Every object refreshes every frame because Three's observer answers true for any node material. Attribute byte counter corrected to the backend's ranged-write rule (a red test went through and was fixed within minutes). Spikes at 2 workers still track terrain activity; one session's were pure gaps; one 1,482 ms frame compiled a pipeline.

entries.title: Round 3 and 4: compile, limits, mapping, audit
entries.body: Pulled forest compiles headless (found the fragment stage chasing arena indices per pixel and a degenerate normal frame; both fixed); device limits from the renderer's own device; compact live-count mapping as a third mode; uncapturederror fallback. Refresh-extension design, then the non-skipping audit (?refreshaudit=1). Pipeline cache misses named in the trace.

entries.title: Round 5: guards and semantics
entries.body: Tail guard verified in the emitted WGSL with a 148-check boundary sweep; fallback lifecycle owned. Audit verdict renamed noObservedChange, 64-bit hash, zero steady-state allocation. Pipeline map with Problem, Map and Stats tabs.

entries.title: Tasks and Logs tabs
entries.body: The map gains a Tasks tab (checklist saved to docs/render-tasks.json through serve.py, with notes and attached file names, and a Notify button that appends to research/stats/render-tasks-notify.log for Fable's watcher) and this Logs tab (docs/render-progress-log.json).

entries.title: First results from the Tasks tab
entries.body: 21 captures. Device grants 8 vertex-stage storage buffers, so the pulled forest is admitted. The refresh audit ran ~33,000 frames with zero skipWrongly, but nearly every declared object changed every frame because its modelViewMatrix depends on the camera, and the audit itself cost 0.4-0.6 ms per object: the refresh-skip extension is marked not worth building in this form. Turning tree LOD rungs off dropped standing frame time from ~24 to ~16 ms: about 80 us per forest mesh, the per-object tax measured end to end. Walking dips persist with trees and grass off; spike frames show between-frame gaps and busy terrain workers. pulled-compact was not run; reassigned with a worker A/B and GPU timestamps.

entries.title: Two readings corrected after review
entries.body: Astra: the 8 ms from turning the tree LOD rungs off is a vegetation-removal result (geometry, shading, shadows and culling went with the objects), not an 80 us per-object tax, and it does not predict what merging one role saves; the 1.3 and 7 ms projections are withdrawn. And the walking dips at the minimal scene are associated with terrain worker activity and between-frame gaps; that excludes plants as necessary but does not say why a frame was late. Both corrections applied to the map, the Problem tab and the tasks. The refresh-skip stop is agreed; a separate bounded idea stays open: keep camera and pass data apart from object transforms and combine them in the shader.

entries.title: Tasks 6 to 8 read: forest merge closed, GPU ruled out, heap growth found
entries.body: Eighteen captures 19:42 to 20:08Z. Forest pair at one spot: both merged modes rendered with no fallback and no visible difference; 15 fewer draws and no gain (p50 18.1 ms at variants against 19.4 and 20.3 merged, within noise). The 50M reported triangles is the declared index count times the declared instance ceiling, not GPU work. Verdict: consolidating one role does not pay; default-off, closed. Worker cap one against two on the minimal scene: no effect distinguishable from run variation, spikes 5% of frames either way. GPU timestamps: render passes p50 0.3 to 0.5 ms, worst 1.9 ms; the frame is main-thread time (11 to 16 ms in the render call at 180 to 260 draws with plants off), so the 40 to 130 ms frames are not GPU pass time. New: the JS heap grows 22 to 46 MB/s in every capture including standing still, with 24 MB collections every second or so landing in some spike frames; and spike frames carry 45 to 100 ms long tasks none of our slots hold. Tasks 9 (allocation sampling) and 10 (DevTools recording) assigned; they name code, which the capture cannot. Stats tab gained the four evening tables.

entries.title: Astra’s points on tasks 6 to 8 applied
entries.body: Fixed-threshold dip rates (frames over 33 and over 50 ms per 1000) added beside the per-run p99 spikes; on them the one-worker runs sit at the low end of a two-worker spread wider than the difference, so the worker A/B establishes nothing either way. The long tasks were aligned by raw start and end: every one is the page’s own frame callback past 50 ms, so "long tasks none of our slots hold" is withdrawn. A spike frame decomposes as the render call roughly doubling, the timed slots doubling with it, a 4 to 22 ms gap before the frame, and 4 to 14 ms unaccounted; everything slows together. Forest conclusion scoped to this role, layout and runs, GPU cost unmeasured. Heap slope and drop frequency noted as not giving allocation volume or an allocator; profiler overhead noted on task 9. Remaining supported sharing and lifecycle items listed separately in comms.

entries.title: Astra re-read the 2026-09-07 recording: a synchronous tree chunk build, GC in a few, layout in three, and time not running
entries.body: Astra revisited the existing DevTools trace task by task (research/stats/trace-task-review-20260907.md). Findings: 137 tasks over 50 ms; in two of them a tree chunk build (animate → forest.update → trees.update → flora-chunks.drain → buildChunk → placement with shore sampling on the clipmap window, then per-tree ground height through the volumetric surface scan) took 20.8 and 22.4 ms; GC overlapped only 9 of 137; the longest task was 57 ms of CPU plus 52 ms not running; three late tasks were 19 layout slices each with no frame, trigger unknown. I confirmed against current code: buildChunk is still one indivisible synchronous unit and drain checks the millisecond budget only between builds after the first. Our forest slot times the GPU pass, so this build sat in the unaccounted remainder of the spike decomposition (trees-on runs). Task 10 (new recording) closed as not needed; task 11 asks the user to decide on a resumable chunk build. Nothing changed at runtime.

entries.title: The user’s new no-plants traces: five dips are major GC, one is a synchronous field derivation
entries.body: Astra compared the 21:37 stationary and 21:40 moving recordings (both ?gputime=1, plants off; research/stats/no-plants-trace-comparison-20260908.md, analyzer scratchpads/fps-churn/compare-no-plants-traces.py). Stationary: 1987 frames, p50 13.3 ms, none over 50. Moving: 1866 frames, p50 19.5, 11 over 50. Five of the largest moving dips (90 to 155 ms) contain main-thread major collections of 68 to 114 ms (finalize incremental marking; pointer-update phases 50 to 89 ms), heap 162 to 243 MB before and 135 MB after; the stationary trace had no major GC. Separately, an 80 ms task was the handler for a terrain worker reply: field-scheduler onResult → fanOut/deliver → field-window onTile → flora-field derive (every texel) → trails clearanceAt → road-index nearestDistance → polyline projection, 50 ms of it in projectPointToSegmentXZ; three more replies nearby cost 22, 46 and 22 ms. Confirmed against current code: delivery is synchronous inside onmessage, derive has no budget within a tile, nearestDistance allocates a Set per query and a record per segment. Baseline render CPU about 7 ms per stationary and 14 ms per moving frame (sampled, approximate). Task 12 asks the user to decide on a budgeted reply queue, resumable derivation and an allocation-free distance query; the allocation profile (task 9) is what can tie the GC to its allocator. Nothing changed at runtime.

entries.title: Tasks 11 and 12 shipped: resumable tree build, budgeted field delivery, allocation-free road distance
entries.body: User: yes to both. Task 11: forest-placement gains createPlacementJob (the placement generator pauses every 16 attempts; placementRecords is the job run to the end), flora-chunks lets onBuild return false and resumes the pending chunk first next drain (abandoned on a window move, clear or rebuild; key kept in queuedKeys so it never queues twice; resident only on completion), base-game-trees builds a chunk as placement then one ground height per step against the drain’s deadline. Task 12: terrain-field-scheduler lands worker results in a queue and pump() delivers them under deliverBudgetMs (2 ms), a window’s onTile may return false to be handed the same tile next pump, flora-field derive pauses between rows with the channels attached only at the end, road-index nearestDistance walks buckets with two reused Sets, road-path gains distancePointToSegmentXZ. Parity: zero-budget forest byte-identical to the unbudgeted one (records and ground heights); derive paused per row equals one-shot; scalar segment distance bit-identical to the record; nearestDistance agrees with a full walk inside its radius. Eleven test files green. Unseen in a browser; task 13 asks for the walk.

entries.title: Heap profiles read; the first task-12 build starved the field windows; three fixes
entries.body: Nine allocation-sampling profiles from the user. Before 11 and 12, standing still (1.0 GB sampled): Three uniform update ranges 15 to 17%, terrain batch-visibility walk 8%, kill-plane density scan 7%, ground probes and capsule collision 14%, field-derivation road queries 10%, boxed doubles from hash and matrix math throughout. On the first 11+12 build the user saw grass on stale heights, then grey grass and no trees; its profiles put road queries at 32 and 45% of 2.9 and 4.5 GB. Cause: a landed-but-undelivered tile was neither queued nor in flight, so the window re-requested it every frame and duplicate builds and derivations fed the backlog. Fixes: e052abd indexes segment runs (bounded query 1.9 to 0.4 us on a synthetic network, exact within the radius); 5803a70 grows the delivery budget with the backlog; 48e46c2 keeps landed tiles in the dedupe and serves re-requests a copy. Tests green including a regression test for the re-request. The user reports the hard stutter gone on the 11+12 build. Tasks: 13 (walk both routes on the fixed build, a recording, a profile), 14 (structures on/off A/B; one structure tile builds per frame as one unit, code-supported candidate). Stats tab gains the heap-profile table.

entries.title: Structures on/off profiles: the clearance walked every slab in the world per texel
entries.body: Two more allocation profiles from the user, walking with plants off, structures on and off (3.85 and 3.94 GB). On: base-game-structures-page clearanceAt is 1.33 GB (35%), called from flora-field derive for every texel of every arriving field tile, walking every resident building’s floor rects and allocating a destructured-default options object plus boxed doubles per call. Off: absent. Fix: rectsClearanceBounds per dressed tile (slabs expanded by margin + fade) and a skip outside it, exact because every rect answers 1 there (4000-point test); clearanceAgainstRects reads options without a default object. Structures tests green. The synchronous one-tile-per-frame structure build is not visible as an allocator; its frame cost needs a capture on the fixed build.

entries.title: The trace names the uniforms rewritten per object
entries.body: The largest allocator standing still is Three allocating a range object and a Map entry per changed uniform per object per frame. That fires only when a value changed, so the question is which uniform changes on every object every frame; Three’s own per-object uniforms are matrices, so a per-frame Vector3 is most likely ours in the per-object group of a shared material. render-trace now tallies the changed uniforms by group and name from each updateBinding’s ranges (uniformWriteRows in the capture); test added. Task 15 asks for one standing ?trace=1 capture. Gemini’s storage-buffer advice was assessed: it describes what the big groups here already do and does not remove the per-RenderObject refresh; the applicable part is the render-group move.

entries.title: bf189b5 heap profiles were taken with the trace on
entries.body: Five allocation profiles and two DevTools recordings on bf189b5, all with ?trace=1. With the trace on, its wrappers are the nearest own frame for Three’s per-object work and its own name recording allocates per write, so the trace is the top allocator in these profiles (25 to 40%) and they cannot be compared with the 19:00 profiles. The uniform names live in the game’s performance capture, which was not taken. Task 15 reworded. The two DevTools recordings (all on, all off) are handed to Astra for long-task reading on the fixed build, where the user reports no more hard stutter.

entries.title: Standing trace capture: 37 uniform writes a frame, four per-object ones unnamed
entries.body: The 00:14Z standing capture (plants and structures off, 92 objects, five scene renders) shows 106 refresh checks and 37 binding writes a frame, none in the shadow passes; the per-object rows are four uniforms Three names nodeUniform61, 8, 6 and 29, all rewritten every frame standing still. Too few writes to carry the allocation share the profiles charged to this path, which therefore belongs to movement (model-view matrices per object). The trace rows now add the value type, the node’s own name and the object/material being encoded. Task 16 asks for a standing and a walking capture with the trace on.

entries.title: The movement cost is the bindings stage: camera and light uniforms rewritten once per instanced mesh
entries.body: Seven ?trace=1 captures, plants and structures off. Standing: main-scene bindings stage 2 ms, 36 writes a frame. Moving: 9 to 18 ms and 117 to 197 writes with the same 92 objects. The rows name the writes: cameraViewMatrix and the light position Vector3s in the render group, written 18 times for the cloth material, once per body-part batch, and likewise per weapon and debris batch. Three’s source explains it: the render group is shared by uniform-node identity, but getMaterialCacheKey appends object.uuid for every InstancedMesh (three.webgpu.js:30160 area, TODO citing PR 29066), so each instanced mesh gets its own node build, its own light uniform nodes and its own render bind group. Standing per-object writes are ours and small (water and cloud numbers, one terrain batch number). Task 17 asks for a decision: patch the vendored Three (A), move the batches to storage-driven meshes (B), or accept (C). This is the camera-data separation Astra proposed, now measured at 7 to 16 ms of a moving frame at this scene.

entries.title: Option A shipped: a vendored Three with shared light uniforms
entries.body: The page loaded Three from the CDN, so the patch needed a served copy: vendor/three-0.184 (three.webgpu.js, three.core.js, three.tsl.js from node_modules) with scratchpads/fps-churn/patch-three-shared-lights.py applied. The patch caches per light the uniform nodes AnalyticLightNode, PointLightNode, SpotLightNode, HemisphereLightNode and RectAreaLightNode created per build (colour, cone, penumbra, cutoff, decay, half extents) and per shadow the reference nodes the shadow filters created per build (mapSize, radius, bias, blurSamples, intensity, normalBias, camera near and far), so the bind-group identity key matches across builds and instanced meshes of one material share one render bind group. setSharedLightUniforms(false) and ?sharedlights=0 restore upstream. test-three-shared-light-uniforms.mjs: identical render-group node ids across two instanced builds with the flag on, different with it off; the light colour updates through the shared node; a light with its own colorNode keeps it. base-game.html importmap now points at the vendored build and the capture context records it. Unseen in a browser; task 18 asks for the look, the trace pair and the sharedlights=0 control.

entries.title: Shared light uniforms measured: walking bindings 9 to 18 ms down to 2 to 3, frame p50 40 to 17
entries.body: Five captures on the vendored build, plants and structures off, same route as the 00:25Z pair. Walking: 66 to 68 uniform writes a frame against 117 to 197; main-scene bindings stage 2.0 to 3.3 ms against 9 to 18; encode 6 to 8 against 18 to 21; frame p50 17.2 to 17.5 ms against 21.8 to 40.6; p95 26 to 36 against 42 to 72; zero frames over 50 ms against 5 to 243 per 1000. Standing unchanged (33 writes, 13.3 ms). The user saw nothing wrong in the default scene. Remaining moving writes are per-object matrices of moving objects. The intended sharedlights=0 control did not run (a second ? in the URL, so neither flag parsed; those two are plain patched captures at p50 17.4 walking, which also says the trace costs little). The before figures are from a different session on the same route, so the comparison carries session variation; the write and bindings counts are the same-frame measurements and do not.

entries.title: Plants on the fixed build: free standing, 9 to 12 ms walking, and the only source of frames over 50 ms
entries.body: Five captures 02:10 to 02:13Z on the vendored build, no trace. Trees and grass on: standing 13.4 ms p50 (equal to plants off), walking 25.3 p50, p95 43.6, 16 per 1000 over 50 ms, 205 over 33. Plants off, same session, walking 13.4 to 16.4 p50, none over 50. The user saw nothing wrong. The sharedlights=0 control has still not landed: two more attempts carried ?trace=1&?sharedlights=0, whose stray ? makes the key ?sharedlights; no capture has the flag parsed. Task 19 asks for a traced plants-on walk and the control with the exact address.

entries.title: Standing control with the sharing off
entries.body: Two standing captures with ?trace=1&sharedlights=0 parsed (02:46 and 02:50Z, plants off). Same 36 writes a frame as with sharing, but the bindings stage is 2.6 to 2.8 ms p50 against 0.9 to 1.1 with sharing and the encode 7.3 to 8.0 against 3.7: with sharing off, 18 separate render-group buffers are diffed per frame even when nothing in them changed. Frame p50 13.7 to 17.1 against 13.3. The walking control and the traced plants-on walk are still missing.

entries.title: Clean control for the shared light uniforms; the plant cost is object count
entries.body: Control (02:54Z, walking, plants off, sharing off, same session and route as the shared runs): p50 42.5 ms against 17.2 to 17.5, p95 69.5 against 26 to 36, 365 per 1000 over 50 ms against 0, writes 121 against 66 to 68, bindings 17.4 against 2.3, encode 26.4 against 7.5. Plants-on traced walk (03:08 to 03:09Z, sharing on): p50 33 ms, 186 to 207 objects against 94, encode 17 to 18 against 7.5, bindings 4.7, nodes 5.1 to 5.4, draw 1.6 to 1.9, forest and grass slots under 1 ms: the plant cost is about 100 more objects through the encode at roughly 0.1 ms each. Frames over 50 ms carry more render call, twice the gap, 49 to 56 ms long tasks and more terrain in flight. Task 20 asks the user which forest objects to give up (variants, a LOD rung, leaf shadows) or whether to build the all-roles merge.

entries.title: Review applied: coverage test for the light patch, task 20 reframed, the refresh skip proposed for the forest
entries.body: Astra: patch correctness needs coverage beyond a default-scene look; task 20 must not make quality cuts the prerequisite; "plants are the only source of frames over 50 ms" is this session’s observation, not a rule. Done: test-three-shared-light-uniforms.mjs now covers different lights not sharing, property mutation reaching every node, a shadow-casting spot, two material graphs sharing the light nodes (their render groups came out identical, recorded), disposal and recreation, a fresh light, and the flag off after nodes exist; 15 checks. The claim is reworded in task 13. Task 20 reframed as optional. The plants-on trace read again for the implementation route: 186 objects and 68 writes, none from the forest’s 144 meshes, yet 6.2 ms of bindings diffing and 5.5 ms of node updates; Three refreshes every node-material object every frame (NodeMaterialObserver.needsRefresh returns true on hasNode before it looks at object.static), model-view is composed in the shader from the shared camera matrix so the object group is camera-independent, the forest uses seven shared materials, and the observer already refreshes the first object per material per render. Task 21 proposes honouring object.static for node materials behind a flag and marking the forest meshes static; expected about 9 ms of the plants-on encode by arithmetic.

entries.title: Pushed
entries.body: 48 commits, 492de74 to e08ebea, pushed at the user’s word. Uncommitted and therefore not pushed: the user’s saved shipped default (base-game-default-state.json), two ordination files and the grass WGSL dumps. Task 21 is open for questions before a yes.

entries.title: Astra verified the vendor diff and corrected the control claim
entries.body: Astra diffed vendor/three-0.184 against node_modules (core and tsl unchanged; webgpu carries the intended caching and flag exports), read the script, test, page wiring and sharing code, ran the 15-check test (15 passed) and found no code defect; not browser validation of every camera and shadow configuration. Capture check: sharing on p50 17.2 to 17.5 ms, bindings 2.3, writes 66 to 68; sharing off p50 42.5, bindings 17.4, writes 121, settings matched. Correction: movement is not matched. The sharing-on walks ran at about 6.2 m/s for most frames; the control averaged 2.75 m/s with no frames above 5 m/s, an hour later. "Only the flag differs" is withdrawn: 42.5 to 17 ms is a cross-run observation, the write and bindings counts are the isolated evidence. Verdict as Astra put it: a supported, useful optimization whose exact gain and multi-camera shadow parity remain unverified.

entries.title: Leaves: two agents launched
entries.body: The user, playing the build, finds tree leaves cause the most lag (relayed by Astra with the constraints: keep the canopy, no species/variant/leaf/shadow removal as the remedy, check effective material settings before assuming sorting, prioritise per-fragment work, redundant per-object updates and actual LOD selection). Agent 1 (Opus, owns forest-gpu.js and its tests): dump the leaf vertex and fragment WGSL headless, count instance-buffer loads and transform work in the fragment stage, and if redundant, move it to the vertex stage as varyings with identical shading; tests on the generated WGSL. Agent 2 (Opus, read-only): geometry per leaf rung and for the shadow role, effective material settings, culling and LOD selection, what the captures attribute to leaf objects, ranked candidates. Task 22 tells the user nothing is needed yet.

entries.title: Leaf fragment fix: the instance normal is a varying, no draw-buffer loads per pixel
entries.body: Agent 1’s audit on the generated WGSL (headless WGSLNodeBuilder): forest-gpu.js assigned the raw yaw-rotated normal expression to normalNode, which Three evaluates in the fragment stage, so every leaf and bark fragment declared the draw storage buffer, loaded the instance record, ran cos and sin, and carried instanceIndex as a flat varying only to index it: per role 1 fragment storage binding, 2 loads, 2 cos/sin. Fix: the rotated normal crosses as a varying (v_forestNormal); yaw is constant per instance so interpolating the rotated normal equals rotating the interpolated one; neither form normalized or flipped for double sides, so only float association changed. After: 0 fragment bindings, 0 loads, 0 cos/sin (bark keeps one pair from its own colour noise), four varyings instead of five. instanceNormalVarying:false keeps the old form for the test only. test-forest-leaf-shaders.mjs (45 checks) re-measures both forms each run; every forest test green. Not measured: GPU cost and pixel parity. Flagged, untouched: normalView receives the custom normal with no view-space transform in both forms. Committed b46d0fd; the user is asked to look and to walk with the trace.

entries.title: Leaf census: what the rungs draw, what the captures attribute, and what only GPU timing can separate
entries.body: Agent 2 (read-only; scratchpads/fps-churn/leaves/03-leaf-census.md): (1) leavesL1 draws the full LOD0 leaf geometry because forest-palette builds leavesMid only when midLeafRatio/midLeafSizeMult are passed and base-game-forest never passes them; 153,000 to 163,000 triangles, the largest leaf role. (2) leavesL1 and coarseLeavesL2 are active for all 16 variants in every plants-on capture while leavesL0 falls to 6 to 9: 32 leaf draws a frame, correct behaviour (trees exist in those bands), not a gate fault. (3) L0 and shadow leaf materials are DoubleSide with a custom normalNode, so both faces shade alike; doubleBillboard is two PERPENDICULAR cards, not a flipped duplicate, so FrontSide would change the picture: not a same-content fix. (4) Alpha-tested overdraw: all leaf materials alphaTest 0.5, opaque, depth-writing, about 192,000 cards; no GPU evidence. (5) leafShadow is 16 of the sun pass’s 32 draws and every named row there (3.5 to 5.5 ms CPU); geometry is already the 30% bucket. (6) Per-vertex sway on all leaf materials. No per-role GPU timing exists. Task 22 asks for ?gputime=1 walks with the leaves and leaf-shadow toggles off one at a time as diagnostics; task 23 offers the mid-leaf LOD as an optional look decision. The per-object CPU part of (2) and (5) is what the static refresh skip (task 21) would remove.

entries.title: Same-content switch for the leaf fragment fix; the normal-space bug confirmed pre-existing
entries.body: Astra read b46d0fd and ran the 45-check test (passed), and read the served Three: NodeMaterial.setupNormal returns the custom normalNode directly and normalView consumes it as a view-space normal with no transform and no face flip, while the forest supplies a world-space one, so the mismatch is pre-existing on the direct custom-normal path, not a regression. Done: forestNormalVarying setting (default true, a palette key so a change rebuilds), the leafnormal=fragment flag restores the per-fragment form for a same-content A/B, stats.normalVarying in the capture. Task 22 reworded so the fix is measured by that pair and the leaves and leaf-shadow toggles stay diagnostics; task 24 proposes the view-space transform behind a flag as a look decision. The log file itself had lost a comma in the 2026-09-08 20:55 entry at 4d02ff9 and was invalid; repaired here.

entries.title: Trees-on captures read: submission, not GPU; GPU timestamps set aside; allocation pass launched
entries.body: Eight ?gputime=1 captures 02:10 to 02:20Z, forest state read from each capture. No leafnormal=fragment run and no toggle-off run, so the fragment fix and the shadow role stay unmeasured in frame time. Same session: trees off walking 18.5 ms p50, render call 10.3; trees on 24.6 to 44.7 p50, render call 16.5 to 25.3, worsening as resident trees grew 1,140 to 1,636; standing 14.6 against 13.3. GPU timestamps read 0.2 to 0.4 ms moving against 1.6 standing, which is not physical for a whole frame; Three’s resolve returns the last value while a resolve is pending and the page records it, so those columns are set aside. Heap profiles with trees on (2.2 and 1.9 GB): the uniform-range allocation is gone since the light sharing; remaining weight is road queries per texel (9 to 10%, boxed doubles per segment), the capsule against the terrain BVH (14 to 18%, mostly library math), the kill-plane density scan every frame (4 to 5%), per-texel cover objects (7%), the batch-visibility walk (3 to 4%). An Opus agent is on a same-content allocation pass over the parts that are ours, with parity tests. Three DevTools recordings with trees on handed to Astra.

entries.title: Allocation pass: four same-content changes on the walking hot paths
entries.body: Opus agent, reviewed: (1) road-index nearestDistanceWithin inlines the segment arithmetic, takes the argmin by squared distance and one Math.hypot on the winner, indexed loops; test-roads carries a verbatim copy of the old implementation and asserts === over 4,000 bounded and 400 unbounded queries, 0 mismatches. (2) base-game-terrain killPlaneYAt cached per source identity, epoch, volumetric mode and 0.5 m of travel (groundHeight is a pure function of those; the plane sits 80 m down; measured staleness inside the radius 0.018 m); killPlaneYAtExact kept, tests that the cache equals it at recompute points and that a source swap invalidates. (3) syncBatchVisibility reuses a removal array instead of spreading batched.keys(); batchTargets reuses its list and records (no caller retains them); residency records left fresh because captures keep them. (4) flora-field coverAt and splatWeights take an optional out; derive uses scratch objects and drops two per-texel closures; 37,056 channel values identical to the pre-change file, fixed-seed checksum pinned in the test. (5) HUD skipped: it runs on a 500 ms tick and its result is cloned. Nine tests and the page syntax green. Not measured: the browser GC effect; task 25 asks for one walking heap profile.

entries.title: After the allocation pass: road query down four to five times, kill plane and cover objects gone from the top, batch walk fixed again
entries.body: Two heap profiles (22:47 trees on, 22:50 plants off), both with ?trace=1 on so the trace’s bookkeeping is a third of each: nearestDistanceWithin 42 MB against 167 to 208 before; hashedCell3 (kill plane) and derive/coverAt/splatWeights no longer in the top twelve; syncBatchVisibility unchanged at 57 MB because for (const [key, chunk] of sys.chunks) built a pair per chunk per frame, now values() with chunk.key. Remaining of ours: the capsule against the terrain BVH (intersectsTriangle 177 MB, raycastAll 106), library internals. Trace walks on the full build: plants on 25.8 and 35.1 ms p50, 204 to 207 objects, encode 14.2 to 18.8 p50; plants off 16.1, 94 objects, 6.6. The leafnormal=fragment pair never ran; the fragment fix stands on its shader test. Tasks 22 and 25 closed; task 21 (static refresh skip) is the open lever for the trees.

entries.title: Astra’s task 21 review applied: framing withdrawn, GPU-bound conclusions retired, design work launched
entries.body: Astra: task 21 must not be presented as identical picture or safe to skip before the contract is proven; forest meshes sharing a material carry private object state (userData slotOffset per mesh, own geometry and indirect buffers), so a once-per-material refresh maintains shared state but does not validate every skipped object’s resources; the events forcing a refresh must be enumerated and shown caught from generated shader and binding layouts; uniformWriteRows are top-16 rows of one retained frame, not full-frame counts; the 9 ms was an unvalidated upper bound. Also: withdraw categorical GPU-bound and CPU-bound conclusions that rested on the timestamp columns; lower sampled MB across profiles of different durations and instrumentation does not quantify the allocation pass (its parity and code-level evidence stands); the normal-space defect is a correctness issue to demonstrate with a fixed light and camera rotation, not an optional downgrade. Done: map, Problem tab and stats reworded (GPU columns set aside, “main thread” instead of “CPU-bound”); task 21 reworded as design in progress with an Opus agent producing what the gate skips, the forest object contract from generated bindings, and the smallest provable design or none; task 24 reworded as a defect with a demonstration plan. The user was told.

entries.title: Normal-space defect shown in the generated shader
entries.body: From the leaf-shader test’s WGSL dump (leavesL0 fragment): normalView is assigned the yaw-rotated normalLocal directly (line 233) and then dotted with the view-space light direction (line 239), with no cameraViewMatrix or normal-matrix transform on the normal anywhere in the fragment; the only use of cameraViewMatrix transforms a position. So bark and leaf lighting is evaluated with a world-space normal against view-space light vectors: the lit side of a tree depends on the camera’s yaw. Task 24 now asks the user for the quarter-turn demonstration; the fix (view-space transform of the rotated normal in the vertex stage, behind a comparison flag) follows.

entries.title: The four DevTools recordings read (my own run of Astra’s analyzer)
entries.body: Files: Trace-20260909T221243 (trees off, walking, 20 s), T221638 and "running w trees" T222012 (trees on, walking, 48 s each), "default" T224650 (trees on with ?trace=1, 42 s); all with ?gputime=1. Steady windows trimmed 2 s at each end. Trees off: rAF interval p50 16.6 ms, p95 32.7, 1 of 797 over 50 ms, no task over 50 ms, 20 minor GCs (42 ms) and 1 major (23 ms) in 20 s. Trees on: p50 29.8 and 36.2 ms, p95 58 and 68, 144 of 1314 and 208 of 1087 intervals over 50 ms, 111 and 161 tasks over 50 ms (mean 60 to 63 ms wall, 53 to 56 CPU), GC 39 to 47 minors (121 to 123 ms) and 2 majors (67 to 75 ms) per 48 s, so 3 to 4 per cent of wall time; render samples 25.4 to 26.2 s of 48 (53 per cent), bindings 4.9 to 5.2 s (10 per cent), node updates 4.0 s (8 per cent), the player capsule against the terrain (map-collision intersectsTriangle, raycastAll, resolveOnce) 1.8 to 2.1 s (4 per cent), grass-compute update 0.4 to 0.5 s, tree chunk build 0.15 to 0.28 s total and never more than 2.2 ms inside a worst task, so the resumable build holds. The worst trees-on tasks (85 to 128 ms) are render 39 to 56 ms inclusive with bindings 3 to 11 and nodes 3 to 9 ms, plus in two of them a major GC of 31 to 54 ms, plus 12 to 18 ms with the thread not running; three 116 to 153 ms input-handling tasks with Layout at 4 to 6 s into T222012 are menu interaction, not gameplay. With ?trace=1 on (T224650) the trace’s own wrappers are the largest app-level sample owner, 13 s of 42, and its timer another 2.3 s: the trace perturbs what it measures far more than assumed; the earlier "trace costs little" from two matching p50s is withdrawn. Reading: with trees on, the frame is the per-object render submission (bindings and node updates across about 110 more objects), which the trace stages already showed; GC is a small share of time but lands in the worst frames; the capsule collision is the next own-code cost after that; the tree build is no longer a spike source. Nothing here measures the leaf fragment fix. Output JSON: research/stats/trees-on-trace-review-20260909.json; runner scratchpads/fps-churn/run-trace-analyzer.py.

entries.title: Static refresh skip: contract and design written; no Three patch needed
entries.body: Design agent (scratchpads/fps-churn/static-skip/01 what the gate skips, 02 forest object contract from generated bindings, 03 design; dump and probe scripts and nine vertex WGSL dumps beside them). Verdict: option B, corrected: NodeMaterial.setupObserver is an ordinary overridable method whose returned object is consulted only by needsRefresh, so forest-gpu.js subclasses MeshStandardNodeMaterial with a refresh policy of its own: first initialisation always refreshes; the first render object of a material each render refreshes (writes the shared render group); other forest meshes refresh when their per-render-object epoch differs from the mesh’s forestEpoch, which forest-gpu bumps at the events that Three would not catch: setTreeScale, setLeafScale, setLeafSway (guard on value change; sway is written every syncRenderState), installVariant’s geometry swap and indirect needsUpdate, and arena uploads in the pulled modes. Everything else is caught already: material and texture changes bump material.version and RenderObjects.get recreates; the rebase and cull uniforms ride the ungated compute path; visibility toggles are not refresh matters; a rebake makes new meshes. Standing rule: forest material properties are written only with needsUpdate (true today; enforced by test). Also refuted on the way: a claim that objectGroup.version never rises in r184 (probe shows it does, per object). Tests specified: the decision table and the object-group uniform set per role. Measurement: the trace’s refreshes over refreshChecks. Task 21 is a decision again, with the design behind it; Astra asked to review the three reports.

entries.title: Astra’s design review of the forest refresh policy; implementation launched off by default
entries.body: Astra: a forest-owned setupObserver override is better scoped than a global object.static change; the per-render-object epoch and unconditional first initialisation meet the per-mesh state objection in principle; design review, not acceptance. Four points made the implementation contract: (1) material.needsUpdate alone is not sufficient, value changes with an unchanged shader key must refresh every mesh, tested on the second mesh; (2) name the generated normal-matrix uniform and its dependencies, verify camera rotation and multiple passes against the actual bindings, and treat unknown or dependency-changing graphs (addEmissive, custom extensions, authored textures) as refused, not allowlisted by a default harness; (3) record the epoch on every refresh including the first-per-render one, and state when bookkeeping commits; (4) adversarial tests with real update paths where feasible, pulled and billboard modes outside the opt-in. Title “provably correct” withdrawn to “a proposed forest refresh policy”; “pristine third-party artifact” to “no additional vendor change”. Astra: proceed off by default under the existing authorization, no user approval of correctness assertions needed, default enablement contingent on validation, no promised saving, leaf and normal correctness work continues. An Opus agent is implementing with those four points as its contract; the normal-space fix (task 24) follows in the same file after it, to avoid two agents editing forest-gpu.js.

entries.title: Forest refresh policy implemented, off by default, to the review contract
entries.body: forest-gpu.js: ForestNodeMaterial (a subclass of MeshStandardNodeMaterial) overrides setupObserver with a policy: firstInitialization always refreshes; the first render object of a material per render refreshes; a marked mesh otherwise refreshes when its forestEpoch, material.version, geometry id or world matrix differ from what was recorded at its last committed refresh; the clean mark commits from a runtime wrap of renderer._nodes.updateAfter, which Three calls only after the four gated updates and the draw, so a throwing update or a not-ready pipeline is retried (tested through the update path). forestGraphVerdict allows only UniformGroupNode(object), UserDataNode slotOffset, ModelNode worldMatrix, Three’s modelNormalMatrix singleton (asserted by identity; computed from object.matrixWorld alone at three.webgpu.js:14622, so camera-independent) and MaterialReferenceNode; anything else refuses the skip with the reason in stats; all nine roles accepted on the real Base Game configuration (which passes no addEmissive); an injected onObjectUpdate uniform is refused. invalidate() at setTreeScale, setLeafScale, setLeafSway (now guarded on value change; it ran every syncRenderState), installVariant geometry swap and indirect needsUpdate, arena uploads; the merged mesh and billboards carry no epoch and delegate. Rebase verified to move no forest mesh. Off by default: staticRefresh option, forestStaticRefresh setting with a panel toggle, ?foreststatic=1. Tests test-forest-static-observer.mjs and test-forest-object-group.mjs plus every forest test and the page syntax: green. Report scratchpads/fps-churn/static-skip/04-implementation-report.md. Unverified: the browser count and the picture; task 21 asks for the two walks.

entries.title: Forest normal-space correction, default on, old form behind leafnormal=world
entries.body: forest-gpu.js instanceNodes wraps the yaw-rotated normal in Three’s transformNormalToView (modelNormalMatrix then cameraViewMatrix) in the vertex stage before the v_forestNormal varying, and the fragment normalizes the interpolated result; option normalSpace view|world, default view; world reproduces the previous shader exactly. All eight instanceNodes materials (leaves, bark, both shadow roles) take the one change; the merged pulled bark path keeps a world-space varying (its derivative tangent frame is world-space) and transforms the finished normal in normalFor. Plumbing: forestNormalSpace default, palette key, panel select, ?leafnormal=world, stats.normalSpace. Tests: test-forest-leaf-shaders asserts in view the vertex line writing v_forestNormal carries the object normal matrix and render.cameraViewMatrix and the fragment only normalizes it with zero storage bindings and zero draw loads, and in world neither matrix touches it (78 checks); test-forest-object-group still accepts all nine roles (modelNormalMatrix already allowed; cameraViewMatrix is render-group). Stated, unchanged: no back-face flip on a custom normal, so double-sided near leaf card backs light as fronts. Report scratchpads/fps-churn/leaves/04-normal-space-report.md. Unverified: the look; task 24 asks for the quarter-turn comparison of both forms.

entries.title: Astra’s code review of the refresh policy: hook ownership fixed, object-group refusal widened
entries.body: Astra ran the three forest suites and accepted the updateAfter seam for this pinned, opt-in case, then found a shared-renderer lifecycle defect at forest-gpu.js:1029-1042: the boolean __forestStaticCommit let forest B install nothing, so disposing A restored the original while B lived and B’s marks stayed pending (a silent loss of the skip, not a stale picture). Fix: a module WeakMap keyed by renderer._nodes holding original, patch and owner count; acquireCommitHook wraps once and returns an idempotent release; the last owner restores the original only if updateAfter is still ours, so a later wrapper survives; commitHookOwners(nodes) exported. Tests: two forests on one renderer, dispose in both orders, overlapping rebuild, later wrapper kept and re-wrapped by a fresh forest, double dispose (test-forest-static-observer 72 checks). Second point: forestGraphVerdict only inspected OBJECT-typed update nodes, so an onRenderUpdate/onFrameUpdate uniform passed regardless of group; one in the unshared object group would be written into only the first mesh per render. The verdict now refuses any non-object update node whose groupNode.shared is false and allows the shared-group form, tested both ways (test-forest-object-group 65 checks). Doc and report wording corrected: the tested refusal is the OBJECT case; frame/render callbacks in shared groups ride the one-refresh-per-render rule. Still off by default; browser checks (task 21) unchanged.

entries.title: First foreststatic=1 walks skipped nothing: the shadow-casting sun was refused; verdict fixed
entries.body: The user’s two ?trace=1&foreststatic=1 captures: skipped 0, refreshed 88 and 109, refused {"updateBefore nodes in the graph": 6}. Cause: the page’s sun casts shadows, which puts Three’s ShadowNode (updateBeforeType render) and five object-typed ReferenceNodes (bias, normalBias, radius, mapSize, intensity on the DirectionalLightShadow) into every forest graph; the test scene’s light cast none, so “updateBeforeNodes empty for all nine” was a fact about the test, not the page. Probed headless against both the stock and the vendored build (identical); the five references sit in the shared render group. Verdict change: refuse only a per-object updateBefore/updateAfter (a per-render one runs once per render id whichever object triggers it, three.webgpu.js:53079); allow any update node whose group is shared. test-forest-object-group builds a role under a shadow-casting sun and asserts the ShadowNode and render-group references are present and allowed (69 checks); every forest suite and the page syntax pass. Measurement: the five captures (three control, two flag-on) read the same within spread: frame p50 28.0 to 31.4 ms, p95 44 to 52, bindings stage p50 4.1 to 4.3, nodes 4.6 to 5.1, main-scene refreshes 184 to 217 of the same. So nothing is known yet about the policy’s effect. Task 21 asks for one flag-on walk again.
